meta.title: 丁克的代价：50岁想给孩子做防火墙
meta.title_en: The Price of Child-Free: At 50 You Want a Child as a Safety Net

scenes.title_en: Easy when young, regretted at fifty
scenes.context: 讲者指出丁克年轻时容易，到 50 岁遇到风险时会后悔没有孩子这道防火墙。
sentences: 丁克年轻的时候是容易的：今年不要孩子，明年不要孩子，自然而然就丁克了。
Going child-free is easy when you're young: skip kids this year, skip them next year, and you're child-free before you know it.
自然而然就丁克了：child-free before you know it
到了你50岁的时候，上有老、下没有小，身体也不是那么好了。
By your fifties, you have aging parents, no kids of your own, and your health is no longer what it was.
上有老下无小：aging parents, no kids
往往人在这种时候会后悔，早知道就做一道防火墙。
People tend to regret it at that point — wishing they'd built a firewall in advance.
做一道防火墙：build a firewall / safety net
paraphrase: 丁克的成本是时间差→50岁才显现
The cost of child-free shows up on a time lag — at fifty.
防火墙=关键时刻的孩子兜底
A firewall means having kids as a safety net when things go wrong.
scenes.speak: Going child-free is easy when you're young: skip kids this year, skip them next year, and you're child-free before you know it. By your fifties, you have aging parents, no kids of your own, and your health is no longer what it was. People tend to regret it at that point — wishing they'd built a firewall in advance.

scenes.title_cn: 阿姨们最大的精神寄托是孩子
scenes.title_en: For the aunties, kids are the biggest anchor
scenes.context: 讲者分享身边阿姨的经历，孩子是他们最大的精神支撑。
sentences: 我身边的阿姨，他们最大的精神寄托都来自于孩子。
The aunties around me draw their biggest emotional anchor from their children.
精神寄托：emotional anchor
他们在说到自己孩子的时候眉飞色舞。
Their faces light up when they talk about their kids.
眉飞色舞：their faces light up
今天是我儿子帮我挂的号，我儿子说多少钱妈我都给你治了。
"My son booked my appointment today. He said: whatever it costs, Mom, I've got you covered."
帮我挂号：booked my appointment
paraphrase: 孩子的价值→不只是养老，是日常心理支撑
Kids matter not just for care, but for daily emotional support.
眉飞色舞→精神寄托的具体化
The glowing faces show what real emotional anchor looks like.
scenes.speak: The aunties around me draw their biggest emotional anchor from their children. Their faces light up when they talk about their kids. "My son booked my appointment today. He said: whatever it costs, Mom, I've got you covered."

scenes.context: 讲者指出可以寻求信仰等替代支撑，但多数人还是靠孩子，需强大的心理或物质能力。
sentences: 那我们可以寻求其他支撑，比如信仰上的支撑。
We can seek other kinds of support, like faith.
信仰支撑：support from faith
没有孩子未必是件坏事情，佛教也这么说。
Being childless isn't necessarily a bad thing — even Buddhist teachings say so.
未必是坏事：isn't necessarily a bad thing
你要么有足够强大的心理支撑能力跟物质能力，否则压力会使你不堪重负。
You need either rock-solid emotional support or real financial strength — otherwise the pressure will crush you.
不堪重负：will crush you
paraphrase: 替代支撑存在→但门槛高
Alternatives exist, but they demand a high bar.
心理与物质→至少一项强大
You need strength in at least one: mind or money.
scenes.speak: We can seek other kinds of support, like faith. Being childless isn't necessarily a bad thing — even Buddhist teachings say so. You need either rock-solid emotional support or real financial strength — otherwise the pressure will crush you.

practice: Skip kids this year and next, and you're child-free before you know it.
I wish I'd built a firewall — a couple of kids as a safety net.
Their children are their biggest emotional anchor.
Without strength on either side, the pressure will crush you.
pitfalls: ✕ 直译腔：Child-free is easy when young.
✓ 地道说法：Going child-free is easy when you're young.
go child-free 是表达「丁克」的常见说法。
✕ 直译腔：Build a fire wall in advance.
✓ 地道说法：Build a firewall — a safety net — in advance.
firewall 已引申为「防火墙、兜底」，可加 safety net 解释。
✕ 直译腔：Their spirit rests on children.
✓ 地道说法：Their kids are their biggest emotional anchor.
emotional anchor 表达精神寄托更地道。
✕ 直译腔：The pressure makes you can't carry it.
✓ 地道说法：The pressure will crush you.
will crush you 简洁有力。
shifts: 丁克=年轻时想清楚就行
丁克=把50岁后的代价也算进来
孩子更多是日常的精神支撑
未必是坏事，但需要替代支撑或强大实力
